title: Sliding Window Pattern
content: The sliding window technique maintains a range of elements and moves the range through the input instead of repeatedly examining the same elements.
intuition: Sliding window is useful when the problem asks about a contiguous subarray or substring and the window can be expanded or contracted while maintaining some property.
approach: Maintain left and right boundaries. Expand the right boundary as new elements are considered. When the window violates a condition, move the left boundary until the condition is restored.
mistakes: Moving the left pointer when the window should expand.
Forgetting to update the answer after changing the window.
Using sliding window for a problem that does not have the required contiguous structure.
space_complexity: Usually O(k), depending on the auxiliary data structure.
